children: Bitcoin is having a rough November. Matthew Sigel is unbothered.

VanEck's head of digital assets research went on CNBC shortly after the US midterms and repeated his bullish case for Bitcoin. He made it as markets fretted over Democratic gains in Congress, a scenario widely labeled a "blue wave." Bitcoin is currently trading around $60,000. By mid-November it was down about 24% from its pre-election high, so his timing took some nerve.
Sigel's argument starts in an unexpected place. He suggested a Democratic-led Congress could help Bitcoin, not hurt it.

His reasoning runs through fiscal policy. On CNBC, Sigel said rising government spending and debt issuance under a Democratic majority could benefit Bitcoin. In his view, that would limit its long-term risk compared with other assets.

Sigel didn't brush off the recent weakness. As of mid-November, Bitcoin had been bouncing between $58,000 and $65,000. He blamed that slide on liquidity tightening and a few other short-term pressures.
One of those pressures came from outside crypto entirely. Sigel cited the Anthropic IPO as a factor weighing on the market.
Sigel leaned on a historical comparison to back his view. He pointed to the 2022 midterms, after which Bitcoin rallied by approximately 300%.
He argued that the setup then resembles the one now. He noted similar Federal Reserve rate conditions and earlier market crises that shaped where Bitcoin went next.
Sigel also pointed to on-chain data, the activity recorded directly on Bitcoin's public ledger. Specifically, he flagged a metric called NUPL, short for net unrealized profit/loss.
Sigel said NUPL currently sits in the "Hope/Fear" zone. His read is that long-term holders are not capitulating, even as liquidity dries up.
His analysis also draws on Bitcoin's four-year cycle. That pattern loosely tracks the network's halving events, when the reward for mining new coins is cut in half.
Sigel's comments fit with VanEck's broader house view on Bitcoin. The firm has forecast a $100,000 Bitcoin price by 2027, tied to its cycle models.
The firm sees two main catalysts on the road to 2027: institutional adoption and regulatory certainty.
VanEck has skin in the game here. As an asset manager with digital asset products, it benefits when investors grow more comfortable with crypto.

The on-chain signals are worth watching closely. If NUPL slides from "Hope/Fear" into capitulation territory, Sigel's claim that long-term holders are holding firm would come under pressure. A move back toward the top of the $58,000 to $65,000 range would support his argument that the selloff was temporary.
VanEck has named regulatory clarity as a key catalyst. How the incoming Congress approaches digital asset rules could shape whether the 2027 target looks prescient or optimistic.

title: VanEck's Matthew Sigel stays bullish on Bitcoin after the midterms
